text: This course's goal is stated plainly: by the end, you should be able to read an existing PowerShell script, understand what it does, modify it safely, and run it — not write a 500-line module from scratch.

If you've used bash or cmd.exe, the biggest adjustment is this — PowerShell's pipeline passes real objects between commands, not plain text. That's what makes a script more reliable than one silently depending on a text format never changing.
Checking a fleet of servers for configuration drift, automating a routine maintenance task across many databases, connecting to Azure resources without clicking through the Portal every time.
Basics, then objects and pipelines, then scripts and control flow, then PowerShell specifically for Azure and SQL. Next up: the console, ISE, and VS Code.
